# A merge keeps the primary, deletes the secondary, and answers with the survivor

**Claim.** The secondary named in the path is merged into the primary named in the body. The 200 carries the primary's vanId — the survivor, not the id from the path — with a Location pointing at it, and the secondary answers 404 from then on.

Applies to: `~1people~1{vanId}~1mergeInto/put`

## Observed exchange

_Two duplicates of one person. The primary survives; the secondary is consumed._

```http
(setup) POST /people/create

{
  "firstName": "Lena",
  "lastName": "Voss-{scope}"
}

→ 201
  Location: https://api.securevan.com/v4/people/100000001
{
  "vanId": 100000001,
  "status": "Stored"
}
```
```http
(setup) POST /people/create

{
  "firstName": "Lena",
  "lastName": "Voss-{scope}"
}

→ 201
  Location: https://api.securevan.com/v4/people/100000002
{
  "vanId": 100000002,
  "status": "Stored"
}
```

_The secondary goes in the path; the body names the primary that survives._

```http
PUT /people/100000002/mergeInto

{
  "vanId": 100000001
}

→ 200
  Location: https://api.securevan.com/v4/people/100000001
{
  "vanId": 100000001
}
```

_The primary is still there under its own vanId._
